 W.P.(MD).Nos.5507 of 2016, 10
 Prayer:

Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution o  to issue a writ of Declaration, declaring that the Tamil Nadu High   2001 (Tamil Nadu Act No.34 of 2002) and its rules 2003 framed there  as unconstitutional under Article 254 of the Constitution of India   inconsistent, repugnant, redundant and unworkable in view of the  commencement of new central Act, The Right to Fair Compensation an  Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement A  2013 (Act No. 30 of 2013).
 For Petitioner : Mr.L.G.Sahadevan  for Mr.V.Manohar  For Respondents : Mr.T.Amjad Khan  Government Advocate  COMMON ORDER (Order of the Court was made by S.M.SUBRAMANIAM,J.)

Today, when these Writ Petitions are taken up for hearing, the learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondents relied upon the decision of the Supreme Court of India in G.Mohan Rao and others Vs. State of Tamil Nadu and others reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 440, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD).Nos.5507 of 2016, 10262 and 13006 to 13009 of 2018 wherein, it has been held that the 2019 Act is to be a legitimate legislative exercise and to be consistent with and within the four corners of Article 254 of the Constitution of India and also of the High Court judgment.

sentences.text: He submitted that the said finding is squarely applicable to the present case also.
2. The learned counsels appearing for the petitioners have not refuted the said submission.
3. In view of the decision cited supra, these Writ Petitions stand dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.

(S.M.S.,J.)
